perspective:
From John Atcitty’s perspective, he has access to the following information:

- He is John Atcitty, an Alaska Native man, a Heavy Equipment Operator with a middle-school education. He teaches equipment operation at a community center.
- He knows Beverly Yan as a colleague at the community center. She teaches adult education classes, and he knows she has a doctorate. He experiences mutual respect with her, and they have collaborated before on projects combining practical and theoretical knowledge.
- During a joint class project, John set up the equipment for the day’s demonstration and hoped it met Beverly’s expectations. He felt insecure about his educational background compared with Beverly’s doctorate.
- He heard Beverly say she admired how he handles machines, that education is not just about degrees, and that it is about what you can do with what you know.
- After Beverly praised his expertise in operating machinery, John felt more confident. He thanked her for her kind words and suggested a new collaboration: a workshop combining theory and practice.
- He heard Beverly say she loved the idea, that his practical skills were invaluable, and that they could create something special together.
- After their successful collaboration, John worried Beverly might now have higher expectations, which made him feel pressured.
- John told Beverly he was worried he might not always meet the high standards they had recently set. He heard Beverly say she appreciated his honesty, wanted realistic goals, and believed their combined efforts—not perfection—made projects successful.
- After that frank discussion, John believed Beverly valued his honesty and saw him as a reliable partner, which enhanced his sense of worth.
- John told Beverly he was glad they had that talk, that he felt he could be open with her, and that it mattered to him. He heard Beverly say she respected his openness, trusted his judgment completely, and wanted to keep the transparency going.
- Encouraged by their successful collaborations and mutual respect, John felt ambitious. He proposed a larger community-wide event to showcase what they had achieved together. He heard Beverly call it a fantastic idea, say it was the perfect way to demonstrate the impact of their work, and agree to start planning.

John does not have access to Beverly’s private thoughts, her personality type, or any narrator-only information unless it was stated or shown through her words and actions.
